title: Match bank payments to invoices by reference

blocks.text: Every morning the accounts team runs the reconciler over the bank's statement file. It matches each payment to the open invoice whose reference the payer typed, and sends the rest to a person for manual review. The team's tests pass, but in production almost every payment ends up in manual review, the run sometimes dies halfway through, and once a payment with no reference at all was booked against an invoice.
`readStatement` and `match` already work. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/Reconciler.java`:

items: `sameReference(invoiceRef, paymentRef)`: whether a payment with that reference pays an invoice issued with that one.

cases.says: a payment is matched to the open invoice that carries its reference, and a payment with an unknown reference is not matched
payments read from the bank's statement file are matched to their invoices
an open invoice issued without a reference doesn't stop the run, and the payments after it are still matched
a payment without a reference is not matched to an invoice without one

origin.section: == Compares References; equals Compares What the Class Defines

concepts: == on references is true only for one object: string literals and compile-time constants share one object, while strings built at run time are new objects, so equals compares the text.
A reference that may be missing has to be checked before a method is called on it; equals on a null receiver throws.
